chunks: And I asked him about a woman who made her wealth an offering for the House of Allah if she lent some belongings to so-and-so and so-and-so, but then some of her family lent them without her permission. He said:

There is no offering due upon her. The offering is only that which is made for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as an offering for the Ka'bah; that is what must be fulfilled when it is made for Allah. As for things resembling this, they are nothing, and there is no offering where the name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is not mentioned in it.

key_terms.لِبَيْتِ ٱللَّهِ: for the House of Allah, meaning the sacred sanctuary
key_terms.لِلْكَعْبَةِ: for the Ka'bah as the intended sacred destination of the offering
key_terms.هَدْيًا: an offering dedicated sacrificially for the sacred sanctuary
key_terms.يُوفَى بِهِ: it must be fulfilled and carried out as an obligation
key_terms.ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ: the name of Allah, whose explicit mention is required here for validity
key_terms.ٱلْهَدْيُ: the legally recognized offering dedicated to Allah

ai.seo_question: When is a hady or vowed offering to Bayt Allah legally valid in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a contingent dedication is not binding in this case, because the act occurred without the woman's authorization. It further clarifies that a valid hady is only what is explicitly made for Allah عز وجل and designated for the Ka'bah, and that such a dedication must include the name of Allah.
